note: Lumen (formerly CenturyLink, ticker CTL until 2020) has renamed its own XBRL extension namespace and re-tagged the same balance-sheet lines three times in fifteen years, so the global bindings catch only part of its history. What needs overriding here is intangibles: Lumen prints TWO lines under goodwill and the global single-element binding takes whichever one it matches, dropping the other -- blank for FY2011-FY2016 and understated by $1.9-2.0B for FY2017-FY2019. Net PP&E was also bound here originally; it is now a global metric (the coverage audit found the same gap in 91 of 118 S&P 500 names), with the identical two elements, so the company-tier copy was removed rather than left to shadow it. Everything else -- revenue, the cash-flow statement, goodwill, equity -- resolves correctly from the global tier and is deliberately left alone.

metrics.label: Customer relationships, net
metrics.note: The larger of the two intangible lines Lumen prints beneath goodwill. Tagged in the company's own ctl: namespace through FY2013 and with the us-gaap concept from FY2014; the two agree exactly in FY2014 ($4.89B on both), so the series joins without a step. Capped at FY2019 because from FY2020 the company stopped splitting this line out and prints only the combined total (see intangibles_total_reported) -- without the cap the two eras would both resolve in FY2019 and the sum below would double-count.

metrics.label: Other intangible assets, net
metrics.note: The second intangible line on the face of the balance sheet, $1.5-2.2B every year. This is the one the global binding drops on the floor: it binds intangibles to a single element, so whichever line it matches, the other is silently lost.

metrics.label: Other intangible assets, net (combined)
metrics.note: From FY2020 Lumen reports one combined intangibles line instead of two. Scoped from FY2020 rather than taken wherever it appears: the company tagged it in FY2019 as well, alongside the two split lines it superseded, and that year is the cross-check rather than a third input -- $7.60B + $1.97B = $9.57B against the $9.57B combined total the company itself tagged. That agreement is what licenses summing the split lines for the years where no combined total exists.

metrics.label: Intangible Assets
metrics.note: Sum of whichever presentation the year used; the from/to scoping above makes the two eras disjoint, so exactly one of (split lines) or (combined total) contributes in any year and nothing is double counted. Restores FY2011-FY2016, which the global binding left blank altogether, and corrects FY2017-FY2019, where it reported only the customer-relationships line and understated intangibles by $1.9-2.0B. That fed straight into tangible book value and unlevered net tangible assets, and for a company whose equity has been reduced to roughly zero by $22.3B of goodwill impairment, a $2B error in the tangible-asset base is not a rounding difference. The FY2011 floor is deliberate: both of Lumen's FY2010 filings fail to parse (one returns 404 for its FilingSummary), so FY2010 resolves only the smaller of the two lines from a later filing's comparative column. Summed, that produced a confident $0.62B for a year the company reported billions of customer-relationship intangibles. Scoping the era out leaves FY2010 blank, which is the honest answer.
